# fastf 3.1.1 — installing on Debian, Ubuntu and any other Linux

A packaging release. The tool is unchanged from 3.1.0.

## A Debian package

Every release now carries a `.deb`, so `apt` owns the files and can take them away again:

```bash
ver=$(curl -fsSL https://api.github.com/repos/cristocola/fast-folder/releases/latest \
  | sed -n 's/.*"tag_name": *"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')
curl -fLO "https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/releases/download/$ver/fastf-$ver-amd64.deb"
sudo apt install "./fastf-$ver-amd64.deb"
```

It installs `fastf` on your PATH along with the man pages, the completions for bash, zsh and fish, a desktop entry and the icons, and `sudo apt remove fast-folder` removes all of it. The package carries the statically linked build, so the same file installs on an old Debian derivative and a current one alike.

The release workflow builds the package from the same staging directory it builds the tarball from, so the two always contain the same thing. It then installs the package on a runner, runs what it installed, checks the man page and the completions landed, and removes it again, which means a package that fails to install fails the release.

## One command for any Linux

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cristocola/fast-folder/main/packaging/linux/install.sh | sh
```

The script downloads the static release archive, checks it against the release's own `SHA256SUMS`, and unpacks it under `~/.local`: the binary, the man pages, the completions, the desktop entry and the icons. It runs as you and writes only inside your home directory, and it says at the end whether `~/.local/bin` is on your PATH. `FASTF_VERSION` pins a release and `PREFIX` chooses where it goes.

The script is [`packaging/linux/install.sh`](https://github.com/cristocola/fast-folder/blob/main/packaging/linux/install.sh). Read it before you run it.

## Also in this release

Every asset now carries a signed build provenance attestation, the `.deb` included:

```bash
gh attestation verify fastf-v3.1.1-amd64.deb --repo cristocola/fast-folder
```

## Upgrading

Nothing to do. If you installed 3.1.0 by hand, either install method above replaces it in place.
